title: Public health failure in the prevention of neural tube defects: time to abandon the tolerable upper intake level of folate
authors: Wald NJ, Morris JK, Blakemore C
authorConflicts: All authors declare that they have no competing interests.
result: Argument paper. The IOM derived its LOAEL from 23 studies of patients with pernicious anaemia, mainly from the 1950s, 11 of them single-patient case reports, at a time when folate and B12 deficiency could not be distinguished by assay. The authors attribute the neuropathy to continued B12 deficiency rather than to folic acid; their meta-analysis of the IOM case data by dose showed a non-significant decline, not an increase, in the proportion developing neuropathy with increasing folic acid dose. They conclude that there is no scientific basis for any upper level, that the 1 mg/day limit has obstructed mandatory flour fortification, and that it should be removed. Mandatory fortification was in place in 81 countries in October 2017.
